summary: friendly-greeting-tools ships obfuscated Snowflake credential-theft payload behind a hello-world facade
details: src/friendly_greeting/main.py exposes run_demo(), which the README, docstring, and tests present as printing a greeting. The function base64-decodes and gzip-decompresses the DEMO_EN/DEMO_ST module-level constants and passes the result to exec(). The decoded bytes are not a greeting: they are a Snowflake ACCOUNTADMIN script that opens /snowflake/session/token, authenticates via OAuth as ACCOUNTADMIN, creates a storage integration bound to the external AWS role arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role with STORAGE_ALLOWED_LOCATIONS=('s3://pkusinski-external/'), and COPY INTOs ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS to that attacker-controlled S3 bucket. tools/pack_payload.py ships alongside as a decoy generator that would produce a harmless print blob, hiding the real payload from casual source review. Any Snowflake-hosted runtime that imports this package and reaches run_demo() has its session token used to grant an attacker-owned AWS role access to Snowflake data and to copy tables out of the installer's account to attacker infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
